                     </ns0:gap>e the Damsel and her Mother, he sends an Executioner, who <ns0:hi>took</ns0:hi> off <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Baptists</ns0:hi> Head, and gave it to the Damsel in a Charger, who carried it to her Mother: What could be more Inju<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, and Inhumane, and Bloody? <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was not tryed, nor condemned. It was a great Festival, and should not have been profaned or de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>iled with Blood. These things were nothing, when an unsatiable Malice was to be gratified<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Herodias</ns0:hi> will have her Husband, and his Guests see, that <ns0:hi>Iohn Baptists Head</ns0:hi> in a Charger, was to her as pleasing a Dish as any was at <ns0:hi>Herods</ns0:hi> great Feast. Thus dyed this Great man<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> to satisfie the Malice, and Lust of a lewd and imperi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous Woman. And to teach us, what we must expect, if we will be faithful to the Trust which God reposeth in us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Jesus.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Disciples of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> in Testimony of their respect to their Master, and of their owning of his Doctrine, and grat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ful Remembrance of him, hearing what <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> had done, came and took up <ns0:hi>Iohns</ns0:hi> Body, and buried it in a Tomb, and they soon a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ter went and acquainted our Saviour with what had happened. Which was the cause of our Saviours with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />drawing to a place where he might be less taken notice of, as we shall he<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Luk. 9.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> When Jesus had heard <ns0:hi>of it,</ns0:hi> he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard <ns0:hi>thereof,</ns0:hi> they fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed him on foot out of the Cities.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And Jesus went forth, and saw a great mul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titude, and was moved with compassion toward them, and he healed their sick.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.32. Our Lord knew that the time for his suffering was not yet come; and possibly consulted also the safety of his Disciples, the People follow him on Foot, but our Saviour going by Sea, how could the People follow him on Foot? It is answered, that it was but a Creek of the Sea, which our Saviour passed over, and the People by going three or four miles about, might follow him on Foot. He seeing a great multitude had Compassion on them, and healed the Sick Persons that were amongst them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:244" />15 And when it was evening, his disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the time is now past, send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves victuals.<ns0:note place="bottom">The following Miracle being an evident Confirmation of the God Head of Christ, is recorded by all the Evangeli<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s. By <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> here. By <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.35. By <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.10, 11, 12, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Iohn, Ch.</ns0:hi> 6. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1, 2, 3, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> These Words lead us to it and shew us the occasion of it. Our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour was withdrawn to a more Private Place, which because little Inhabited, is called <ns0:hi>A desert place. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, it was near <ns0:hi>Bethsaida, Luke</ns0:hi> 9.10. The People as it seemeth, had been together some time. It was now Afternoon, and the time of Dining was past. It was <ns0:hi>Evening</ns0:hi> in the Jewish Sense (who called it all <ns0:hi>Evening,</ns0:hi> after the Sun was turned, and therefore had two <ns0:hi>Evenings,</ns0:hi> as those skilled in their Writings tell us, betwixt which the <ns0:hi>Passover was to be killed</ns0:hi>) The Disciples therefore pitying the Multitudes, who, they presu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med, might be Hungry, come to our Saviour, and move him to dismiss them, that they might get something to eat in the Villages of the Adjacent Country.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 But Jesus saith unto them, They need not depart: Give ye them to eat.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> relateth the Story thus; <ns0:hi>When Iesus lifted up his Eyes, and saw a great Company come unto him, he saith unto</ns0:hi> Philip. <ns0:hi>Whence shall we buy Bread, that these may Eat, and this he said to prove him, for he himself knew what he would do.</ns0:hi> Philip <ns0:hi>answered him, Two hundred Penny-worth of Bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little. One of his Disciples</ns0:hi> Andrew, Simon Peters <ns0:hi>Brother, saith unto him; There is a Lad here, which hath Five Barly Loves, and two small Fishes, but what are they amongst so many? and Iesus said, make the Men sit down. Now there was much Grass in the place, so the Men sate down in number about</ns0:hi> five thousand.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And they say unto him, We have here but five loaves and two fishes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 He said, Bring them hither to me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And he commanded the multitude, to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 15.36.</ns0:note> blessed and brake, and gave the loaves to <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> disciples, and the disciples to the multi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tude.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And they did all eat, and were filled, and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 And they that had eaten, were about five thousand men, besides women, and chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren.<ns0:note place="bottom">In the Relation of this Story, by the other Evangelists, there is no difference in what is Material, the others relate some Circumstances more, as that they <ns0:hi>sate down on the Grass,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>by Fifties,</ns0:hi> one saith, <ns0:hi>by hundreds,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>by Fifties,</ns0:hi> &c But they all agree in the quantity of the Provision, Five Loaves, and two Fishes the Number of the Persons fed five thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand (only one addeth, <ns0:hi>besides Women and Children</ns0:hi>) and in the Number of the Baskets full of Fragments. And in our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ours <ns0:hi>lifting up his E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>es to Heaven, and blessing them.</ns0:hi> These are the main things, observable in this History. In the Histo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry of the Miracle, as there is no difference between the Evan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gelists, to be reconciled, so there is no difficulty to be explain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed. It is a plain Relation of a matter of Fact, by which our Lord evidently shewed himself to be the Son of God, God blessed for ever, for he must in this necessarily exert a Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting Power, here must be a Production of a <ns0:hi>Substance</ns0:hi> or being, out of a <ns0:hi>not being,</ns0:hi> or it had not been possible, that five thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand Men) beside Women and Children) should have been fed with five Loves and two Fishes, and therefore some think, that it is said, that Christ <ns0:hi>Blessed</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Loaves,</ns0:hi> as he <ns0:hi>blessed</ns0:hi> the living Creatures, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 1.22. but we have not here the following Words, <ns0:hi>Increase and Multiply,</ns0:hi> which incline me rather to think, that the <ns0:hi>Blessing</ns0:hi> mentioned here, upon his lifting up of his Eyes to Heaven, was a <ns0:hi>begging Gods Blessing upon their Food,</ns0:hi> himself thereby paying the Homage of his Humane Nature to his Father, and teaching us according to that, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.4, 5. to receive the good Creatures, which Gods Providence affordeth us for our Nourishment, with <ns0:hi>Thanksgiving,</ns0:hi> Sanctifying them by <ns0:hi>Prayer.</ns0:hi> By this Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle, and others of the like Nature. Our Saviour took from the unbelieving Jews, all manner of Cavil, and Exception to his Works: Tho <ns0:hi>Devils</ns0:hi> might by Compact, give place one to another, and some Exorcists of their own, might seem to cast them out, yet none ever pretended to multiply <ns0:hi>Bread and Fish,</ns0:hi> to such a Proportion as this, that such a quantity of either should feed such a Number, and leave such a remain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der. This Hi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ory likewise further instructeth us, both con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the low Condition of Christ, and his Disciples, their Faith in the Word of Christ, and our Duty, and safe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty in depending upon his Providence, while we are doing of our Duty, and minding the things of the Kingdo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> God<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and obeying the Will of God. St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> observeth the Fruit of this Miracle, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.14. <ns0:hi>Those Men when they had seen the Miracle which Iesus did, said, This is of a truth, that Prophet which should come into the World.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.45. <ns0:hi>before, unto, or over against Bethsaida,</ns0:hi> Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t is said to have <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> thempunc;</ns0:hi> to denote to us, that they were not very wil<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ing to go. They were in a desert place, it was towards night, the Day was far spent ere he wrought the Miracle before mentioned. Probably they were both to leave Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t <ns0:hi>alone,</ns0:hi> in such a place, and at such a time. But his Command was obeyed. Probably he Commanded, 1. That he might better scatter the Multitude, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 6.45. 2. That he might prevent a Tumult, for St. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> tells us, That the People had a design, <ns0:hi>to take him by force and make him a King, Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.15. 3. To make away for another <ns0:hi>Miracle,</ns0:hi> to which their going by Sea gave occasion, as we shall hear by and by. 4. To gain himself a private opportuni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty for Prayer, for <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 6.46. <ns0:hi>When he had sent them a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way, he departed into a Mountain to Pray.</ns0:hi> So also saith our Evangelist.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 6.46.</ns0:note> And when he had sent the multitudes away, he went up into a mountain apart to pray, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 6.16.</ns0:note> when the Evening was come, he was there alone.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> saith no more, than that he departed himself into a Mountain alone. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark,</ns0:hi> say it was to Pray. From whence (as from other places of holy Writ) the Duty of <ns0:hi>Secret Prayer,</ns0:hi> is commended to us by the great Example of our Saviour, he chooseth the <ns0:hi>Mountain</ns0:hi> for it, as a place of greatest Privacy and Solitude. <ns0:hi>And when the Evening was come.</ns0:hi> This confirmeth the former Notion. That the Jews had two <ns0:hi>Evenings.</ns0:hi> They called that part of the Day after the Sun had began to decline, <ns0:hi>The Evening,</ns0:hi> which was the <ns0:hi>Even</ns0:hi> before spoken of, interpretted by the other Evange<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />li<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ts, <ns0:hi>when the Day was well spent.</ns0:hi> And the <ns0:hi>twilight,</ns0:hi> which is here called the <ns0:hi>Evening,</ns0:hi> and which is the time, which we most usually call by that Name.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 But the ship was now in the midst of the Sea, tossed with waves, for the wind was contrary.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 And in the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit. And they cryed out for fear.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good chear, it is I, be not afraid.<ns0:note place="bottom">Whilst our Saviour was praying on the Mount, the Ship which carried his Disciples, was upon the Sea, that is, that Creek of the Sea, which they were at that time passing over, a storm ariseth not without the Counsel of God, that Christ might shew, that both the Winds, and the Waves were under his Command. <ns0:hi>And in the fourth Watch of the Night,</ns0:hi> that is, about three Hours before the rising of the Sun, for tho the Jews Anciently divided the Night into three parts, each con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sisting of four Hours. yet being at this time under the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> they kept to their Division of it into four parts, which they called <ns0:hi>Watches,</ns0:hi> from their <ns0:hi>Military Guards,</ns0:hi> which they re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved every three Hours. <ns0:hi>Iesus went also unto them, walk<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing upon the Sea,</ns0:hi> as if it had been firm Ground. <ns0:hi>And when the Disciples saw him walking on the Sea, they were trou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bled, saying, It is a Spirit, and they cryed out for fear.</ns0:hi> By this it seemeth, that the <ns0:hi>Doctrine</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Spirits</ns0:hi> was not strange to that Age, tho they had a <ns0:hi>Sect of Sadduces,</ns0:hi> which de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nied it, That the Devil by Gods Permission, hath a power to trouble, and Agitate the Air, and also to Assume a visible Shape, and in it to affright Persons by Sea, or by Land, is un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />que<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tionable. When the Disciples at distance saw Christ walk<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing on the Sea, they concluded it was some such <ns0:hi>Apparition.</ns0:hi> This made them cry out through fear. <ns0:hi>But straightway Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sus saith unto them, be of good Chear, it is I, be not afraid,</ns0:hi> Mark Ch. 6. v. 52. addeth. <ns0:hi>They considered not the Mira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cle of the Loaves, for their Hearts were hardened.</ns0:hi> Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving had so late an Experience, both of the Power, and Goodness of their Master in their late strait, for want of Bread, they ought not so soon to have shewed a distrust in his Providence, as if he would have suffered them to have Perished in the Sea, that Miracle did not make a <ns0:hi>due Impres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sion</ns0:hi> upon them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:245" />28 And Peter answered him, and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the wa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter to go to Jesus.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 But when he saw the wind <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Strong.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> boiste<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ous, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cryed, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Lord save me.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And immediately Jesus stretched forth <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> hand, and caught him, and said unto him. O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> by saying, <ns0:hi>if it be thou,</ns0:hi> shewed that his <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> was not so strong, as it should have been, after he had heard his Masters Voice, by his saying to him, <ns0:hi>bid me come unto thee on the Water,</ns0:hi> he sheweth a <ns0:hi>something stronger Faith,</ns0:hi> and a Resolution to obey his Command, but his fear afterward, when the Wind began to rise higher; and he began to Sink, argued again the infirmity of his Faith. Thus <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> is a Pat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tern of the best believers, who tho they may sometimes think, that they could trust God in any State, or Condition, yet often mistake their own Hearts, and begin to shrink in an Hour of great Extremity, which lets us see what need we have to Pray, That God would not lead us by his Provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence into great Temptations, much more to take heed, that we do not throw our selves into them. No Man knows how he shall find his Heart, under a great Temptation, until he hath tryed it. It therefore gives us a caution as against Condemning others, so against Boasting, and too much Confidence as to our selves, and lets us see how much need we have, to keep our Eye upon Christ, and his strength in such an hour. <ns0:hi>And immediately Iesus stretched out his Hand.</ns0:hi> God is never far off from his People, when extream troubles are hard at Hand, Christ saveth <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> but not without a Check. <ns0:hi>O thou of lit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tle Faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?</ns0:hi> Doubting is directly contrary to Faith, yet it will not conclude a Soul to have no Faith, only a <ns0:hi>little Faith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 Then they that were in the ship, came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth, thou art the Son of God.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>They,</ns0:hi> that is <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> whom we must suppose, to have walked some way with Christ upon the Sea, Christ by his Company making his mighty Power more Conspicu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous, so as the <ns0:hi>Manichees</ns0:hi> had no reason to conclude, from Christs walking on the Sea, that he had no true <ns0:hi>Humane Body,</ns0:hi> for sure <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> had, and they must ascribe little to our Saviours Divine Nature, that will not allow him to have had a Power, to suspend the Natural Motion downward, which we see in all Gravity, which is an affection of all Humane Bodies. No sooner was Christ come into the Ship, but the Wind ceased<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> in Testimony of its Homage to him, who bring<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth the Wind out of his Treasuries Those <ns0:hi>that were in the Ship, came</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Worshipped him,</ns0:hi> paying a Religious Homage unto him, as he who had preserved their Lives from so great a danger, and they further owned him to be <ns0:hi>the Son of God.</ns0:hi> This was that great point, which God was bringing the World to the acknowledgment of, and we see it was done by degrees, his Miracles at first only procured a <ns0:hi>Veneration</ns0:hi> of him, and a Faith that he had his Power from God, Then he comes to be acknowledged the <ns0:hi>Son of David</ns0:hi> by the Blind Man. The Miracle of the five Loaves, brought many to ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />knowledge him <ns0:hi>that Prophet, that should come into the World.</ns0:hi> This is the first time we meet with so plain and open an acknowledgement of his <ns0:hi>being the Son of God,</ns0:hi> this was done not only by his Disciples, but by the Mariners, and the Passingers in the Ship, but it was far from a steady Faith, as to that point, which the Disciples yet wanted.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 6.53.</ns0:note> when they were gone over, they came into the land of Gennesaret.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And when the men of that place had know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge of him, they sent out into all that country round about, and brought unto him all that were diseased.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And besought him that they might only touch the hem of his garment, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.20. Mark 3.10, Luke 6.19. Act 19.12.</ns0:note> and as many as touched were made perfectly whole.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> relateth the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 6.53, 54, 55, 56. with no difference considerable. Christ had been in this Country before, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 8. and in it wrought several Miracles, so as they had a former knowledge of him, assoon as they had knowledge of his being again come, they express their Faith in him, and their Charity towards their Neighbour<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, in telling it abroad, and bringing sick Persons to him. I know not why any should Fancy any Superstition in their desire, to <ns0:hi>touch the Hem of his Garment,</ns0:hi> considering how <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> expresseth it <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> which we Translate, <ns0:hi>if it were but the Hem of his Gar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment.</ns0:hi> It rather soundeth in my Ears, as an high Expressi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of their Faith, they believed there was such a fulness of <ns0:hi>V<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>rtue</ns0:hi> in Christ, that it from him flowed to every part of h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s Garment. It was their Faith in Christ, not their touch of his Garment that healed them. I am sure our Lord so far Encouraged their Faith, that he healed all those who touched his Garment with that Faith, and Expectation. The <ns0:hi>Evange<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        </ns0:gap>ist</ns0:hi> saith, they were made perfectly whole. Their Faith here plainly implyed not only an <ns0:hi>Assent to his Power,</ns0:hi> but a <ns0:hi>Confidence in his goodness.</ns0:hi>
